counterfactual_missing_items: No Toxoplasma serology or CSF PCR is reported
No CD4 count or HIV test is reported
No documented response to anti-toxoplasmosis therapy
decisive_items: Three well-defined lesions within right basal ganglia and medial aspect of right superior frontal gyrus
keeping cats as pets at home
response.rationale: R3 best explains the highly specific CNS pattern with an immunocompromised host and cat exposure: multiple ring-enhancing basal ganglia/supratentorial lesions. R4 is the closest alternative because the same brain lesions could be tuberculomas, but it lacks raw spans linking the pulmonary syndrome to TB and does not explain cat exposure. R1/R5 account only for pulmonary features, while R7 and R6 lack the defining brain lesion pattern or immune-recovery context.

rejected.why: Raw spans support pulmonary TB but do not account for the multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions.
Supported by hypoxia, dry cough, and oral thrush, but fails to explain the CNS imaging findings.
No evidence of ART initiation or immune reconstitution is provided.
Only cachexia and weight loss are cited; no skin/mucosal Kaposi lesions are described.
